author: Amara Okafor
title: HTML & CSS Foundations
description: Build a solid base for web pages: structure with HTML, style with CSS, then lay it out with Flexbox.

sections.title: HTML structure
sections.description: Tags, elements and the skeleton of a web page.

questions.text: Which tag holds the visible content of a web page?
questions.feedback: <body> contains everything the user sees.

questions.text: Which tag creates a hyperlink?
questions.feedback: The anchor tag <a> with an href attribute makes links.

questions.text: Which tag defines the largest heading?
questions.feedback: <h1> is the top-level heading; <h6> is the smallest.

questions.text: What does HTML stand for?
questions.feedback: HTML is HyperText Markup Language.

sections.title: CSS basics
sections.description: Selectors, properties and styling text and colour.

questions.text: Which property changes the colour of text?
questions.feedback: color sets the foreground (text) colour.

questions.text: Which selector targets elements with class "card"?
questions.feedback: A dot selects classes; a hash selects ids.

questions.text: Where should you link an external stylesheet?
questions.feedback: <link rel="stylesheet" href="…"> belongs in the document head.

questions.text: Which property adds space outside an element's border?
questions.feedback: margin is outside the border; padding is inside.

sections.title: Layout with Flexbox
sections.description: Arranging items in rows and columns.

questions.text: Which declaration turns an element into a flex container?
questions.feedback: display: flex enables Flexbox on the parent.

questions.text: Which property aligns flex items along the main axis?
questions.feedback: justify-content distributes items along the main axis.

questions.text: What is the default value of flex-direction?
questions.feedback: Flex items sit in a row by default.

questions.text: Which property lets flex items wrap onto new lines?
questions.feedback: flex-wrap: wrap allows items to move to the next line.

author: Daniel Mensah
title: Personal Finance 101
description: From budgeting to credit: the money basics everyone should know, taught one step at a time.

questions.text: In the 50/30/20 rule, what is the 20% for?
questions.feedback: 50% needs, 30% wants and 20% savings or paying down debt.

questions.text: A budget compares which two things?
questions.feedback: A budget plans how income is spent.

questions.text: Which is a fixed expense?
questions.feedback: Fixed expenses stay the same each month, like rent.

questions.text: What is the first step in making a budget?
questions.feedback: You can only plan spending once you know what comes in.

sections.title: Saving and emergency funds
sections.description: Building a safety net and making money grow.

questions.text: How big is a typical emergency fund target?
questions.feedback: Many advisors suggest three to six months of essential costs.

questions.text: Where should an emergency fund be kept?
questions.feedback: It should be safe and available quickly.

questions.text: What does "pay yourself first" mean?
options: Set savings aside as soon as you're paid
questions.feedback: Saving before spending makes it automatic.

questions.text: Interest earned on previously earned interest is called…
questions.feedback: Compounding lets savings grow faster over time.

sections.title: Credit and debt
sections.description: Understanding credit scores and paying off what you owe.

questions.text: What do lenders use a credit score for?
options: Estimating how likely you are to repay
questions.feedback: It summarises your credit history.

questions.text: Which habit usually lowers a credit score?
questions.feedback: Late or missed payments hurt your score.

questions.text: What does APR stand for?
questions.feedback: APR is the yearly cost of borrowing.

questions.text: Which method pays off the smallest balances first?
questions.feedback: The snowball method builds momentum with quick wins.

author: Quiz Club
title: World Capitals
description: Ten capital cities that trip people up. How many can you name?

questions.text: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.feedback: Canberra was purpose-built as the capital.

questions.text: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.feedback: Ottawa sits on the border of Ontario and Quebec.

questions.text: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.feedback: Brasília replaced Rio as capital in 1960.

questions.text: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.feedback: Tokyo has been the capital since 1868.

questions.text: What is the capital of Egypt?
questions.feedback: Cairo is on the Nile.

questions.text: What is the capital of Kenya?
questions.feedback: Nairobi is Kenya's largest city and capital.

questions.text: What is the capital of Turkey?
questions.feedback: Ankara, not Istanbul, is Turkey's capital.

questions.text: What is the capital of Nigeria?
questions.feedback: Abuja became the capital in 1991.

questions.text: What is the capital of Argentina?
questions.feedback: Buenos Aires lies on the Río de la Plata.

questions.text: What is the capital of Switzerland?
questions.feedback: Bern is Switzerland's federal city.

author: Priya Nair
title: General Science Mix
description: A quick mixed round of biology, chemistry and physics essentials.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.feedback: Au comes from the Latin word aurum.

questions.text: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.feedback: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun.

questions.text: Which gas do plants absorb for photosynthesis?
questions.feedback: Plants take in CO₂ and release oxygen.

questions.text: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.feedback: Diamond tops the Mohs hardness scale.

questions.text: Which organelle is the "powerhouse" of the cell?
questions.feedback: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's ATP.

questions.text: Roughly how fast does light travel?
questions.feedback: Light travels about 300,000 kilometres per second.

questions.text: Which force pulls objects towards the Earth?
questions.feedback: Gravity attracts masses towards each other.

questions.text: How many bones does an adult human have?
questions.feedback: An adult skeleton has 206 bones.

questions.text: At sea level, water boils at…
questions.feedback: Water boils at 100 °C (212 °F) at standard pressure.

questions.text: Which blood cells carry oxygen?
questions.feedback: Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds oxygen.

author: Lena Fischer
title: English Grammar Essentials
description: Spelling, tenses, punctuation and word choice in ten quick questions.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
questions.feedback: They're is short for "they are".

questions.text: What is the plural of "child"?
questions.feedback: Child has an irregular plural: children.

questions.text: What is the past tense of "go"?
questions.feedback: Went is the simple past; gone is the past participle.

questions.text: Which word is a noun?
questions.feedback: Happiness names a feeling, so it is a noun.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
questions.feedback: With she/he/it we use doesn't.

questions.text: Which punctuation mark ends a question?
questions.feedback: Direct questions end with a question mark.

questions.text: Which word means the same as "happy"?
questions.feedback: Joyful is a synonym of happy.

questions.text: Which shows possession correctly?
questions.feedback: Add 's to show that the book belongs to Sarah.

questions.text: What is the opposite of "ancient"?
questions.feedback: Modern is the antonym of ancient.

questions.text: An adjective describes…
questions.feedback: Adjectives modify nouns, e.g. a red car.
